extracted.intended_audience: microbiologists, bacterial taxonomists, nomenclature committee members, type culture collection curators
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and formal opinions governing conservation, rejection, and formation of names of prokaryotic taxa (families, genera, species, subspecies, classes, orders), plus rules about type species/strains and name-formation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LIST 1. Conserved and rejected family names
rubrics_metrics.description: Conserved and rejected family names (nomina familiarum conservanda et rejicienda). The Appendix provides conserved family names, names of type genera of conserved families, rejected names, opinion numbers, and citations (e.g., Enterobacteriaceae conserved; Bacteriaceae rejected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a formal list with columns: Conserved name (nomen conservandum), Name of type genus of conserved family, Rejected name (nomen rejiciendum), Opinion no., Citations. Examples/citations included (Opinion 15; citations 8:73–74 (1958), 32:464–465 (1982), etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: LIST 2. Conserved names of genera of prokaryotes
rubrics_metrics.description: List of conserved generic names (nomina generum conservanda) with the name of the type species of the conserved genus, opinion numbers, and citations (e.g., Aeromonas Stanier 1943 — type Aeromonas hydrophila; Bacillus Cohn 1872 — type Bacillus subtilis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each conserved genus entry includes the conserved generic name, name of type species, opinion number and literature citations; used as the formal record of names to be retained despite competing synonyms or prior usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: LIST 3. Conserved specific epithets in species names of prokaryotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Conserved specific epithets (epitheta specifica conservanda) listing epithets conserved in particular species (e.g., acidilactici conserved in Pediococcus acidilactici; cholerae conserved in Vibrio cholerae), with opinion numbers and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the formal conservation of particular specific epithets in specified combinations, including opinion numbers and bibliographic citations; used to stabilize species names against competing synonyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: LIST 4. Rejected names of genera and subgenera of prokaryotes
rubrics_metrics.description: List of rejected generic or subgeneric names (nomina generum et subgenerum rejicienda) including the rejected name, names of type species (if any), opinion number, notes (reason such as later homonym, nomen dubium, nomen confusum), and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries specify why a generic name is rejected (e.g., later homonym of a protozoan generic name, nomen dubium, no species listed). Examples: Bacterium Ehrenberg 1828 recognized as a nomen generum rejiciendum; Astasia Pribram 1929 later homonym of Astasia Ehrenberg 1830 (Protozoa).

rubrics_metrics.name: LIST 5. Rejected specific and subspecific epithets
rubrics_metrics.description: List of specific and subspecific epithets rejected for use in prokaryote names (epitheta specifica et subspecifica rejicienda) with the rejected epithet, the species in which it was rejected, opinion number and citations (e.g., pestis rejected in some combinations; anaerobius listed with Opinion 56).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides formal record of epithets to be rejected, with citations and notes; includes examples and cross-references to Opinions and subsequent reconsiderations (e.g., Opinion 75 supplement reevaluations).

rubrics_metrics.name: LIST 6. Rejected names of classes of prokaryotes
rubrics_metrics.description: List of rejected class names (nomina classis rejicienda) with the names (e.g., Acidobacteria Cavalier-Smith 2002, Alphabacteria Cavalier-Smith 2002), opinion number (79 supplement) and citations (64:3599-3602 (2014)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal list indicating class-level names judged invalid/rejected by the Commission; includes opinion references and publication citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: LIST 7. Rejected names of orders of prokaryotes
rubrics_metrics.description: List of rejected order names (nomina ordo rejicienda) with names (e.g., Acidobacteriales Cavalier-Smith 2002, Actinoplanales Cavalier-Smith 2002), opinion number (79 supplement) and citations (64:3599-3602 (2014)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal list indicating order-level names judged invalid/rejected by the Commission; includes opinion references and publication citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and maintenance of type species and type (standard) strains
rubrics_metrics.description: Type species and a type (standard) strain are to be designated for genera/species and cultures of the type strain together with complete description should be maintained at each recognized Type Culture Collection (e.g., Bacillus: type species Bacillus subtilis Cohn 1872; type (standard) strain = Marburg strain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion A specifies (a) designation of a genus as conserved, (b) designation of the type species, (c) designation of the type (standard) strain, and (d) requirement that cultures and complete descriptions are to be maintained at recognized Type Culture Collections. Use these designations to fix name application and ensure availability of type material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimitation of genus by diagnostic biological property (example: Bacillus endospore production)
rubrics_metrics.description: A genus may be formally defined so as to exclude species lacking a key diagnostic feature (e.g., Opinion A: the genus Bacillus should be defined so as to exclude bacterial species which do not produce endospores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissions may define genera by phenotypic/diagnostic criteria to preserve taxonomic clarity; examples and resulting taxonomic actions are recorded in Opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation of generic name usage from morphological terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic names should be used as formal names distinct from morphological/common terms (e.g., 'Bacillus' as generic name is to be differentiated from the terms 'bacillus', 'bacille', and 'Bazillus' used as morphological designations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion A explicitly recommends using the generic name in its taxonomic sense and avoiding confusion with morphology-based common nouns or variant spellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic homonyms prohibited; avoid cross-kingdom homonymy
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic homonyms are not permitted (Opinion B). It is advisable to avoid homonyms among Protista on one hand and plants or animals on the other; generic homonyms in the group Protista are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names that are homonyms (same spelling used for different genera) are to be rejected/avoided; the Commission records such rejections and conservations to minimize cross-taxonomic confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of specific epithets derived from personal names (historical opinion and current rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion C noted that specific names derived from personal names may be written with a capital initial letter, but this Opinion was later revoked by Rule 59 of the Code; modern Recommendation: 'A specific epithet, even one derived from the name of a person, should not be written with an initial capital letter.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical practice (Opinion C) permitted capitalization; the Code (1958/1966 editions and later Rule 59) revoked that permission—current standard is lowercase initial for specific epithets. The Appendix records the Opinion and the revocation note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stems/combining forms for compound bacterial generic names and corresponding family endings
rubrics_metrics.description: The combining forms (stems) of compound bacterial generic names ending in -bacterium, -bacter, or -bactrum (-bactron) are specified: -bacterium → stem -bacteri; -bactrum/-bactron → -bactr; -bacter → -bacter. Family names derived from such endings have endings -bacteriaceae, -bactraceae, and -bacteraceae respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion provides formal rules for formation of stems and family names from compound generic names; used when constructing family-level names from genus names with these endings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender assignment for bacterial generic names ending in -bacter
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacterial generic names ending in -bacter should be regarded as having the masculine gender (Opinion: gender of bacterial names ending in -bacter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determines agreement of specific epithets and adjectival endings; recorded as a formal Opinion by the Judicial Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of serotype numbers to identify Shigella species strains
rubrics_metrics.description: A culture belonging to Shigella dysenteriae, S. flexneri, S. boydii, or S. sonnei may be completely identified by appending a serotype number (Arabic) to the species name (Subcommittee on Enterobacteriaceae).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical identification convention for strains within those species: append serotype number to species name to indicate serotype; Opinion recommends designation of type cultures for each of the four species and maintenance in Type Culture Collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories/reasons for rejecting names (nomen ambiguum, later homonym, nomen confusum, nomen dubium, illegitimate later homonym)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names are rejected for formal nomenclatural reasons which are recorded in the lists and notes — examples include 'Nomen ambiguum', 'Later homonym of ...', 'Nomen confusum', 'Nomen dubium', and 'Illegitimate later homonym'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejected-name entries include the specific reason and citations; these categories are used by the Commission to justify placement of names in the 'rejected' lists (LIST 4, LIST 5, etc.). Examples: Astasia Pribram 1929 — later homonym; Bacterium Ehrenberg 1828 — nomen generum rejiciendum.
